content.text:
- "0.07% p.a... You don't have to pay them separately." Ok, so the fee is basically nothing. Still no amount in shekels anywhere.
- Enough. It looks good, but I still don't know how I'd actually buy it from here.

**What I decided:** Yeah, worth looking into. It's the big S&P 500 fund from iShares, a name I know. The fee is tiny and it went up a lot. Fairly sure, but I'm not buying today. The yellow warning at the top said it "may not be eligible for acquisition in your country of residence", and nothing on the page tells me how someone in Israel buys it. Next step is asking my bank, or the friends at work, how they bought theirs.

What decided it was the chart: "5 years: +73.19%". In my head that turns 30k into about 50k. Plus "TER 0.07% p.a." and the FAQ line "You don't have to pay them separately".

**How it went:**
- A settings popup came up first. I just hit Save.
- **Top of the page:** price in EUR, a red "-4.82%" for the day that scared me a bit, the yellow warning, and "TER 0.07%".
- **Chart:** 1 year +13.79%. I tapped 5Y and got +73.19%. It was red, below zero, for most of 2022 to 2023.
- **Basics table:** I only noticed the huge fund size and "Fund domicile Ireland". Ireland for an American fund? Weird. I skipped the "Tax status Germany" part.
- **Performance:** the numbers don't match the chart. The table says 1 year +17.05% and 5 years +78.97%, the chart said +13.79% and +73.19%. Which is it? It also says 2022 was -13.30%. I skipped the heat map, just a wall of tiny numbers.
- **Risk:** I didn't read the "Volatility" text. "Maximum drawdown since inception -33.71%" scared me. On my 30k that's like 10k gone.
- **Stock exchange:** a table of codes and exchanges in Europe and London. No Tel Aviv, no shekels. Lost me.
- **Lower down:** another S&P fund at 0.03%, "State Street". Cheaper, but I've never heard of them.
- **FAQ:** I opened "What are the costs…". It was the only fold whose label asked my exact question.

**Words I didn't get:** "Accumulating", "Replication Physical", "Currency hedged", "Volatility", "Return per risk", "Maximum drawdown", "UCITS", "Acc"/"Dist", "ISIN", "Ticker", "gettex", "Market Maker".

**Where I'd have bailed:** around the Stock exchange table. Up to there it was fine, but all those codes, and nowhere did it say what this costs in shekels or how I'd buy it.
